transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO, Osiris), David Kim (Head of MLOps), Sara Ngo (Security)

Summary (auto): Short demo of Model Catalog, focused on selecting open models, reviewing Redwood's benchmark artifacts and compatibility matrices. Discussed hosting modes and security requirements. Agreed next steps around a small benchmark POC and sharing security docs.

00:00 - 00:30 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, I handle the account. With me is Carlos our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:30 - 01:12 Lena: Good, thanks. Excited to see the model catalog. We are evaluating open models for a conversational triage assistant and want to balance accuracy with latency and cost.
01:12 - 01:45 Maya: Perfect. Quick agenda, we'll show model catalog, highlight performance profiles and the compatibility matrix (streaming, function-calling, quantization support), then talk about deployment options: hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC.
01:45 - 02:05 Carlos: I'll kick off the catalog demo, and we'll pause for questions.

02:10 - 03:00 Carlos: (screen) So here's the Model Catalog, we surface curated open models — Lama 2  (note: transcription shows Lama), Mistral 7B, Falcon 40B variants, and a couple of optimized weights. Each has a performance card: latency at typical sequence lengths, tokens/sec, recommended quantization profiles, and whether it supports streaming and function calling.
03:00 - 03:30 David: Quick Q — does your catalog show per-model memory and required GPU types? We're on A10Gs and some T4s in prod.
03:30 - 04:10 Carlos: Yes, each profile lists supported accelerators and an execution footprint. We also show compatibility notes: e.g. Mistral-ish variants run well on A10G with int8 quant, but for 40B Falcons you'd want A100 or H100 for reasonable latency. The matrix flags support for KV-cache persistence, streaming, and function-calling hooks.

04:15 - 05:00 Lena: When you say int8, are you referring to post-training quantization? How much quality do we lose?
05:00 - 06:20 Carlos: Good question, so Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload. For shorter conversation turns, int8 or q4_0 often keeps rouge/accuracy close within a few percentage points but reduces memory and raises throughput. We usually suggest running a lightweight eval on your prompts — our benchmark template captures perplexity-ish metrics (or evaluation hits) plus application-level checks.
06:20 - 07:00 Sara: Security — we will need SOC 2 evidence, SSO integration (SAML), and KMS for key management. Also data residency: logs must stay in us-east-1.
07:00 - 07:50 Maya: We have SOC 2, SAML/SSO, and KMS integrations. For Private deployments you can bring your KMS or HSM and run our control plane in your VPC. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available in Redwood Console. I'll share the SOC 2 and encryption docs after the call.

07:55 - 09:00 Carlos: Back to benchmarks — here's a sample compatibility matrix. Columns: model, streaming, function-calling, quantization supported (q4_0, int8), recommended GPU, typical latency @512 tokens, tokens/sec.
09:00 - 09:40 Carlos: Example: Mistral 7B — streaming yes, function-calling partial (needs adapter), quantization q4_0 works, recommended: A10G or A100 for high QPS, latency often ~90ms for short prompts in Dedicated pools. Falcon 40B — streaming yes, function-calling yes, quantization heavier but possible with H100.
09:40 - 10:30 David: Are these numbers from your hosted infra or internal lab? We need representative numbers for our infra.
10:30 - 11:20 Carlos: Mostly lab with representative hardware; for Dedicated we can run the same benchmark in a capacity slice matching your instance types. That's what we recommend for procurement decisions. We'll provide raw logs and a CSV.

11:25 - 13:00 Lena: Cost — how do you show unit cost? Is it per token? We need to compare running a smaller open model with more queries vs bigger model with fewer API calls.
13:00 - 14:00 Maya: Hosted billing is per-token; Dedicated is a reserved capacity model (monthly commit) and you get unit cost based on utilization. Redwood Console shows token-level cost attribution so you can compare model-level spend. Our Optimize engine also suggests batching and cache TTL to reduce cost.
14:00 - 15:30 David: Hmm, we have a hard latency SLO for triage: 200ms p95. Which models reliably hit that?
15:30 - 17:00 Carlos: For 200ms p95 you'll look at Llama 2 13B / Mistral 7B on A10G with aggressive batching and KV cache for prefixes; Llama 70B variants will struggle. If you need strict p95 latency you probably pick smaller quantized models or Dedicated with guaranteed capacity.

17:05 - 19:00 Sara: For compliance, will the logs include raw customer content? We cannot have PHI stored.
19:00 - 20:20 Maya: By default hosted logs can include transcriptions for debugging but we support log redaction and configurable retention. For regulated data we recommend Dedicated or Private where logs are retained in your VPC and you manage retention policies.
20:20 - 22:10 Lena: Let's talk compatibility for function calling — we rely on structured JSON outputs to map back to our backend. How robust is the model function-calling support?
22:10 - 24:00 Carlos: We have function-calling shims for many models; some open models need light supervision templates to produce stable JSON. The catalog flags 'function-calling: native' vs 'needs template'. We also provide a small evaluation harness to test on your sample prompts.

24:10 - 27:00 David: For the POC, we want to run 3 models: Mistral 7B q4_0, Llama 2 13B int8, and Falcon 40B (if we can afford it). Run the same prompt set, capture latency distribution, token cost, and qualitative outputs.
27:00 - 28:30 Maya: That aligns with our suggestion. We'll supply the benchmark template and a spreadsheet where you can drop your prompts and we'll run them on the Dedicated slice so numbers match your infra.
28:30 - 30:00 Lena: Any blockers for running in our VPC? We have strict egress rules.
30:00 - 31:20 Carlos: For Private we deploy in your VPC or on-prem, no egress by default. For Dedicated there's a customer-managed peering option; we'll work with your infra team on networking.

31:25 - 33:00 Sara: Authentication and role mapping — our admins need RBAC scoped to teams.
33:00 - 34:00 Maya: Console supports SSO+SCIM for provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. We'll share documentation for role mappings.

34:10 - 36:00 Carlos: Quick demo of Console: per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and an example rollout page where you can pin a model version and do a canary. If a newer model fails quality checks the automatic fallback will route to a stable variant.
36:00 - 37:10 David: Nice — for evaluations, can we replay a production trace?
37:10 - 38:40 Carlos: Yes, you can replay traces through our Optimize toolkit; it recommends batching, cache TTLs, and model variants, and estimates cost savings per month.

38:45 - 40:00 Lena: Good. Let's recap next steps.
40:00 - 41:10 Maya: Recap: I'll send pricing grid, SOC2 and encryption docs, and the benchmark template. Carlos will set up a Dedicated benchmark run and share the results. Lena will confirm infra contact and POC window.
41:10 - 41:45 Lena: Sounds good. We'll aim to pick POC dates by Friday.
41:45 - 42:00 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.

Notes: Transcript contains light transcription errors (Lama = Llama, Mistral sometimes spelled Mys-tral) typical of auto-captioning. Shared artifacts referenced during call: link: drive.google.com/benchmark-template (benchmark template), link: drive.google.com/security-pack (SOC2 + encryption docs), link: console.redwood.ai/compat-matrix (compatibility matrix sample).
